- Overestimate prices after recent sentiment spikes (especially +0.44 or +0.36) — model tends to overshoot and fail to correct.
- Underestimate when sentiment is mildly negative (e.g., -0.08 or 0.09) — model ignores downward pressure.
- Lag in response to sentiment shifts: model reacts 1–2 days too late to sentiment turning points.
- Mean reversion bias: model overweights recent highs and fails to revert to 30-day moving average in 3–5 days.
- Overshoot after sharp upward moves: if sentiment peaks >0.36, model often forecasts 5–10% above true outcome.
- Underweight sentiment when it’s weak or flat (e.g., 0.00 or 0.18) — model assumes stability, leading to underforecasting.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are overly optimistic in early 2025, especially when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive.
